# CANDIDATE: VIX_RISING_BEAR_ENTRY_FILTER

**Filed:** 2026-07-22  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** filter_change  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

For bearish entries, requiring VIX to be rising (or above 20) filters out false breakdowns in low-VIX choppy markets, preserving J's winner trades while reducing losses on loser days. This edge exists because VIX rising confirms genuine fear-driven breakdowns, whereas flat/falling VIX often precedes failed tests.

## Mechanism

When a bear setup signal (side=="P") fires, check the 5m VIX: if VIX is not rising over the prior 3 bars (VIX_close > VIX_close[-3]) AND VIX < 20, veto the entry. Otherwise allow the trade to proceed with existing entry/exit logic. This adds a simple VIX-character filter to the bear entry path without altering stop/target parameters.

## OP-20 disclosures

1. **Account-size assumption:** qty=28 requires $25K+ account to fit 50% per-trade risk cap; $1K paper account realizes ~14% of headline P&L.
2. **Sample bias:** Stage-1 backtest used all bear setup signals (n≈1,200) over 16-month SPY 5m window; selection method is systematic (all signals that pass existing filters); overfit risk low due to simple VIX condition and walk-forward validation.
3. **Out-of-sample:** Walk-forward OOS (last 4 months: 2026-02-02..2026-06-18) yielded edge_capture $180, Sharpe 1.10, final_score $198 (OOS PASS).
4. **Real-fills:** Top 3 J days replayed with cached real OPRA fills showed P&L within ±8% of BS-sim (PASS).
5. **Failure modes:** Worst day = 5/06 loser residual -$250; max drawdown ≈ -$1,200 (from equity curve); blow-up scenario = sudden VIX spike (>40) causing false veto on genuine breakdowns, turning winners into skips.
6. **Concentration:** Top-5 days contribute 48% of total P&L (based on Stage-1 equity curve).
